claims.text: Conventional material processing approaches strengthen materials at the cost of reduced ductility.
Machine-learning-based process optimization can overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
Predictive modeling can identify and guide processing conditions that improve strength while preserving ductility.
Machine-learning-optimized processing conditions control grain size and dislocation density.
Controlled grain refinement and dislocation engineering overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The optimized process will increase strength by 20% relative to the baseline.
The optimized process will maintain ductility at no less than 80% of the baseline value.
Predictive-model accuracy and the optimization ability of the machine-learning algorithm may affect the outcome.
A strength increase below 15% or a ductility reduction above 20% relative to baseline falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The predicted strength increase is 20%, but the hypothesis is falsified only below 15%; therefore, results from 15% to less than 20% would fail the stated prediction without meeting the falsification criterion.
